eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Japan Meteorological Agency and ensemble models point to a cloudy August 23 in Tokyo with scattered showers or thundery activity under northeasterly flow, limiting solar insolation and capping afternoon heating near 30–32°C. This aligns with late-August climatological normals around 30.5–31°C while making 33°C or higher unlikely without unexpected clearing. Traders assign nearly equal weight to 30°C and 31°C outcomes because minor differences in cloud cover timing or shower intensity can shift the daily maximum by 1°C, and real-time observations will resolve the exact peak before market settlement.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from official sources like Argentina’s Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) and international models points to a daytime high of 11–13 °C on 23 August 2026 in Buenos Aires.** This narrow band explains why 13 °C holds the largest market share (58.5 %), followed by 12 °C (26.5 %) and 14 °C (14.0 %). 

Recent observations show a cold front cleared on 22 August, leaving high pressure, light southerly to southeasterly winds, and partly cloudy skies that limit daytime heating. Minimum temperatures fell to 4–6 °C overnight, with dry air and modest solar insolation supporting only modest afternoon recovery. Historical climatology for late August places the typical maximum near 12–14 °C, so current conditions sit close to seasonal norms without anomalous warm advection or cloud cover that could push readings higher or lower. 

Model runs and hourly guidance peak in the 11–12 °C range during midday and early afternoon, with limited upside risk unless unexpected clearing occurs. Traders are therefore pricing the outcome tightly around the SMN forecast of 13 °C, with the secondary probabilities reflecting small model spread and measurement uncertainty at official stations.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official National Weather Service forecasts for Denver on August 24, 2026, center on a high near 90–93°F under partly cloudy skies with a 30–40% chance of afternoon thunderstorms.** This positions the market’s leading bins (90–91°F at 44.5% and 92–93°F at 38%) as the most probable outcomes, with traders balancing the core forecast against the moderating effects of potential convection.

Key differentiating factors include solar insolation at Denver’s ~5,280-foot elevation, where clear to partly cloudy conditions allow rapid daytime warming, versus scattered thunderstorms that can develop after noon. Storms increase cloud cover, enhance evaporative cooling, and deliver brief showers or gusty winds, often capping the daily maximum by several degrees if they initiate earlier or become more widespread. Recent model consensus and NWS guidance highlight this afternoon timing window as the primary source of uncertainty, consistent with typical late-August monsoon-influenced patterns in the Front Range.

Historical August variability, with recent days showing highs from the upper 80s to low 90s amid similar storm chances, further supports the tight clustering around 90–93°F. Updated model runs or morning observations on the 24th could shift the distribution if storm coverage or timing changes.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Marcos A. Gelabert Intl Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 24 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=mpmg

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from meteorological agencies for Panama City, Panama, indicate a daytime high near 31–32°C on August 24 amid the wet season, with trader consensus clustering on these outcomes due to typical equatorial conditions. High humidity and light winds further moderate extremes, while model runs show limited spread without major synoptic shifts. Historical August averages near 31°C provide baseline context, with resolution hinging on precise maximum readings from official stations.
